title: Brand Basics — Colors, Fonts, Logo
summary: People remember your perspective before your colors — POV first, design supports it.

sections.heading: Orientation — Lesson Start
sections.subtitle: Lesson Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **What will you understand?** **People remember you by your stance** — **not by your colors**.
- **Visual identity is important** — **but what truly makes people remember you** **is your consistent point of view** **on the topic you discuss**.
- **This lesson focuses on the essence of a Brand:** **a clear stance** **that shows in your words, choices, and presentation style**.

sections.heading: Tension — The Problem
sections.subtitle: The Problem
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Beautiful content in appearance** **but lacks a distinct mark**.
- **Many content creators** **change colors and fonts** — **but no one can say a single memorable phrase about them**.
- **When your stance is unclear** — **the audience sees your content as generic and replaceable** **even if the design is beautiful**.

sections.heading: Core Idea — A Consistent POV = Stronger Memory
sections.subtitle: A Consistent POV = Stronger Memory
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **POV (Point of View)** **is the statement** **that summarizes how you see the world in your field** — **and makes all content align**.
- **Colors serve the POV** **not the other way around**. **First, know your stance** — **then choose a form that supports it**.
- **When your stance is consistent** — **even different topics** **remain connected** **with the same mental identity for the audience**.

sections.heading: Comparison — A Visual Brand or a Brand with a Stance?
sections.subtitle: A Visual Brand or a Brand with a Stance?
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Visual Brand Only | Brand with a Clear Stance |
|----------------|------------------|
| **Organized design** **but the message changes every day** — **people love the look** **but don’t know where you stand** | **A consistent POV drives the content** **and the design supports it** — **people remember you** **by your way of thinking before the look** |

sections.heading: Glossary — Identity Stabilization Terms
sections.subtitle: Identity Stabilization Terms
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| **POV (Point of View)** | **The statement** **that clarifies your unique stance in your field** | «**I am against quick productivity tips** **and prefer sustainable simple systems**» |
| **Brand Promise** | **The promise** **the audience expects from you every time** | «**You will receive actionable steps** **that are easy to implement without complication**» |
| **Consistency** | **Stability of message and tone over time** | **Even with different topics** **the overall stance remains clear** |

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Confirmation
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
> **Quiz key (unchanged):** correctIndex: 1

**Question:** **Your designs are beautiful** **but people can’t say** **what you are known for** — **what's the top priority?**

Change colors weekly** **until you find a style**.**
**Define your POV** **with a clear statement** **before any visual changes**.
Increase the number of posts** **without changing the message**.**

**Explanation:** **True identity starts from the clarity of your stance**. **The form supports the message** **but does not compensate for its absence**.

**Define your POV** **with a clear statement** **before any visual changes**.
Increase the number of posts** **without changing the message**.**

sections.heading: Mission — Write One POV Statement
sections.subtitle: Write One POV Statement
sections.contentMarkdown:
**Introduction:** **The core of the brand:** **one stance statement** **that serves as a reference for all content you publish**.

**Submission:** Field + Audience · A POV statement starting with «I believe that…» · Two content examples · **One statement you won’t say because it contradicts your stance**

**Evaluation Criteria:**

| Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Clarity of the POV | 50% | **The statement is specific and understandable** — **not general for anyone** |
| Translation to Content | 50% | **Two clear examples + a rejected statement** **that confirms the consistency of the stance** |

sections.heading: Confidence Close
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **You understood:** **You now have the statement** **that distinguishes you** **even before people remember your name or colors**.
- **You can:** **Every new content** **must pass one question:** **Does it serve my stance or not?**
- **Next:** **Grid Consistency** — **the consistency of the profile for the new visitor**.
